_comment: Python (pip-audit) vulnerability findings this repo has deliberately decided NOT to fix by upgrading, with the reason recorded here rather than only in a workflow comment. Read by .github/workflows/test.yml's pip-audit step, which turns each "python" entry into a --ignore-vuln flag, and by scripts/npm_audit_gate.py for the "npm" list (npm audit has no --ignore flag, so the filtering is done on the parsed JSON instead). This file exists because test.yml and frontend-tests.yml's own header comments already referenced it as the established escape hatch ('record why it is unreachable in .github/audit-allowlist.json') before it was ever actually built -- CLAUDE.md's own standing rule is to carry a stated decision through to the code that enforces it, not just describe it. Every entry needs an id, package, fix_version (from pip-audit's own output), reason, and added date. A red pip-audit gate for anything NOT listed here still means upgrade the pin -- this file is for genuinely irreconcilable constraints, never a shortcut around one that could just be fixed.

npm.reason: There is no version of braces that fixes this. The advisory range is <=3.0.3 and 3.0.3 IS the latest published release, so npm's own suggested remedy is not a braces upgrade at all -- it is tailwindcss@4, which replaced the globbing engine and dropped the dependency. That is a major migration (Tailwind 4 moves configuration into CSS, so both tailwind.config.js files, the ~930 ramp-referencing classes across the two apps, and src/palette.test.ts which PARSES those configs, all change together) and it is not something to take as a drive-by security fix. The advisory is a stack-exhaustion denial of service triggered by a deeply nested brace pattern. braces reaches this repo only at BUILD and DEV time, through tailwindcss's content globbing (via fast-glob/micromatch) and chokidar's file watching -- it is not in either shipped browser bundle, so no visitor, child, or parent can reach it at runtime. The glob patterns it expands are the ones written in our own tailwind.config.js `content` arrays; an attacker would have to be able to edit this repository's build configuration to supply a malicious pattern, at which point the brace expander is not the problem. Revisit when either braces publishes a fix (which would make this a one-line lockfile change) or the Tailwind 4 migration is taken deliberately on its own merits. Note the four sibling findings npm reports -- chokidar, micromatch, fast-glob, tailwindcss -- are not separate advisories; they are packages that depend on this one, which is why scripts/npm_audit_gate.py allowlists by advisory id rather than by package name.

undici reaches this repository only through @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers -> miniflare, the Workers TEST runtime that license-server/'s workerd signing-proof suite runs on. It is a dev/test dependency exclusively: the shipped artifact is the Worker bundle (license-server/src/** + the stripe SDK), whose production runtime is Cloudflare's workerd -- undici ships to no family instance, browser bundle, or deployed surface. The vulnerable range (<7.29.1) is pinned transitively by miniflare's own dependency; npm's suggested remediation is a semver-major DOWNGRADE of the pool to 0.8.30 (the vitest-2 era), which would abandon the vitest-4 pool wiring the runtime proof needs -- a worse trade than a recorded exception. The exception retires when the next miniflare/pool release bumps undici to >=7.29.1, at which point this file's stale-exemption notice flags the entry for deletion. Scope: license-server/'s toolchain only -- undici is not a dependency of homeschool-tutor or demo.

Same dependency path and remediation reasoning as the GHSA-rfgv-xxqx-mfg5 entry directly above (undici via @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers -> miniflare; dev/test only; workerd is the production runtime; the pool downgrade npm suggests is rejected; retires on the next miniflare/pool undici bump).
